_description: Student's t return distribution with df=6 (moderate fat tails). Accumulation-only scenario with no cash flow, so the portfolio balance at year 15 is purely a product of 15 yearly growth factors. With standardized-t (scaled to unit variance) the expected value and volatility match the log-normal case; only kurtosis differs, producing slightly wider tail behavior but a similar median.
_rationale: 60/40 portfolio starting at $500,000, stockReturn=7% stockStdDev=15%, bondReturn=3% bondStdDev=5%, no correlation, no withdrawals, 15 years. Blended expected return ≈ 5.4%, so deterministic growth is 500000 * 1.054^15 ≈ $1,100,000. With standardized-t (df=6) realized log-space variance matches the log-normal case, so the median should land close to the same range (mid-six-figure to low-seven-figure band). The test simply checks that the t-distribution path runs, produces a sane positive balance, and 100% success over a no-withdrawal run.
name: Fat Tail: Moderate (df=6)
